questions.stem: An air compressor starts unloaded so that it:
options: Keeps the drains closed while it starts
Uses more air at start to cool itself
Cools the receiver before it fills
Gets up to speed before it works against pressure
questions.explanation: The unloader reduces the starting load.

questions.stem: Condensation in an air receiver should be:
options: Drained regularly to prevent corrosion
Left to build up as a seal in the bottom
Drained only at the yearly survey
Mixed back in with the oil for lubrication
questions.explanation: Water in air systems causes corrosion and erratic operation.

questions.stem: Which device protects an air receiver from over-pressure?
options: Drain cock
Sight glass
Pressure gauge
Safety relief valve
questions.explanation: Never alter its setting without authority.

questions.stem: An intercooler on a two-stage air compressor:
options: Removes oil from the cylinder
Cools the air between stages
Drains the receiver
Heats the air before the receiver
questions.explanation: Cooling between stages improves efficiency and lowers final air temperature.

questions.stem: Compared with hydraulic oil, air is:
options: Incompressible, and heats when squeezed
Compressible, and heats up when compressed
Compressible, and cools down when compressed
Heavier and more viscous than the oil
questions.explanation: Air volume shrinks under pressure and the work of compression heats it.

questions.stem: In a piston compressor, air enters the cylinder through the:
options: Discharge valve on the upstroke
Relief valve on the head
Drain valve at the bottom
Suction valve on the downstroke
questions.explanation: The pressure falls in the cylinder on the downstroke, so the suction valve opens. The discharge valve opens when the compressed air exceeds line pressure.

questions.stem: What makes a small compressor start and stop automatically to keep the receiver topped up?
options: The safety relief valve on the receiver
A pressure switch with cut-in and cut-out settings
The automatic drain cock fitted to the receiver
The intercooler between the two stages
questions.explanation: The pressure switch starts the motor when pressure falls to cut-in and stops it at cut-out.

questions.stem: A compressor must never be run with its discharge valve closed because:
options: The suction valve will stick shut
The air will be too cold to use
The intercooler will freeze up
Pressure and heat rise, and oil vapour may ignite
questions.explanation: Without a path out the air heats and pressurises, and carbon and oil can burn.

questions.stem: Compressed air must not be used to blow dust off overalls because:
options: It wastes electricity and nothing more
Air can enter the skin and particles hit the eyes
The oil mist in the air will freeze on the cloth
The dust may catch fire from the air jet
questions.explanation: A jet of air can inject into the skin, and it throws particles into the eyes.

questions.stem: A receiver's safety relief valve keeps lifting. The correct response is to:
options: Screw down the spring to stop it lifting
Fit a blank in its outlet to stop the noise and loss
Find why the pressure is too high and fix it
Leave it alone until it fails completely
questions.explanation: A relief valve is the last protection. Never adjust or jam it. Fix the cause.
